input.title: Provenance brief: the carrier follow misses a birth when the old carrier spells the rule differently
input.body:
Found while backfilling `macos` (#2251). The brief's carrier follow — `followCarrier`, the pickaxe added in #2248 — put two of that pack's rules' `born` at the carrier they moved *into* rather than at their real birth. Both were corrected by hand against `git show`; nothing in the tool would have caught either.

## The two failure modes

**1. A hit that is not a carrier.** `menu-bar-only` was drafted `born` at #915 because the pickaxe's earliest hit for its text was a **README index row**, not the rule. Its real birth is `RULES.md` at #756. The follow takes the earliest commit whose diff contains the needle, and a README table listing the pack's rules contains every needle by construction.

**2. A spelling the pickaxe cannot see — and this one is silent.** `pin-lsminimumsystemversion-same` was drafted `born` at #1667, the commit that *moved* it, and was **not** listed under the brief's "elements older than the carrier they sit in" section at all. The rule's text at the old path carried backticks (`` `LSMinimumSystemVersion` ``) that the needle does not, so the pickaxe found nothing earlier and the follow correctly concluded there was no earlier carrier — from evidence that was never going to match.

Mode 1 produces a flagged derivation a run is told to verify. Mode 2 produces an unflagged one that reads as settled. Mode 2 is the one that ships wrong.

## Why it matters now

Three corpora remain on #2169 and all of them run through this path:

| Corpus | Files |
|---|---|
| `basics` | 133 |
| this repo's local pack | 89 |
| `claudinite-growth` | 89 |

A wrong `born` is not a cosmetic error: it attributes a decision to the wrong pull request, and the entry is append-only, so correcting it later costs a second entry that has to explain the first.

## What a fix has to do

- **Exclude a hit whose file cannot be the carrier.** A `README.md` row, a `VERSIONS.md` row and a catalog table are evidence the element was *mentioned*, never that it was carried there. The carrier kinds are already known to `packCarriers`.
- **Distinguish "no earlier carrier" from "no match".** These are different answers and the brief currently prints neither — it just drafts the later commit as the birth. Where the follow finds nothing, say so beside the draft, so the run knows an unverified assumption is sitting there rather than a derivation.
- **Match a needle whose surrounding markup differs.** Normalising backticks out of both sides before the pickaxe would have caught this one; whether that generalises safely is the open question, and a narrower fix that only reports the uncertainty is worth more than a looser match that invents a different wrong answer.

The second point is the one I would not skip even if the other two prove awkward: a derivation the tool cannot make is fine, and the whole design of the brief is that it hands those over rather than guessing. This is one it guesses at.

## Verification

Reproduce on the real history rather than a fixture — both cases are live on `main`:

```
node packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs brief macos menu-bar-only pin-lsminimumsystemversion-same
```

The first should stop drafting #915 and the second should either derive #756 or say plainly that it could not.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   Three user messages drove this segment:

   - **"lgtm"** — Approval of [PR #2248](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2248) (the four-issue provenance-tool fix). Per the owner's `lgtm-merges` rule this means: merge the change at hand into `main` via the `merge-to-main` skill; it approves that change only, never later work.
   - **"Let's do another 2 packs: macos and research-project. One PR in two subagents (one for each pack) makes sense?"** — Both a command (backfill these two packs' provenance) and a genuine question inviting pushback on the PR/subagent shape.
   - **"lgtm both"** — Approval to merge both resulting PRs, #2251 and #2252.

   Two AskUserQuestion answers also carry decision weight:
   - PR count → **"Two PRs, one per pack (Recommended)"**
   - Model field → **"Record it when possible. Don't force an 'I don't know the model'. Backfill if available."**

   **Standing constraints still in force (preserve verbatim):**
   - "Do not run this on Fable — the owner's standing instruction for this work."
   - GitHub scope is limited to `missingbulb/claudinite`; do not read from, write to, or search across any other repository unless added via `add_repo`.
   - `no-pr-polling`: "never schedule a self check-in to poll it, no recurring wake-up, routine or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads its state, CI or mergeability on a timer; act on PR events when they arrive, and end the turn when none has."
   - Needing a decision or approval → `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose, one question per item, each with its case.
   - "Wanting to re-post a question the owner declined — don't. Take its recommended default, or open the question up."
   - End every turn with a blockquote callout, `> ✅ All done` or `> ⚠️ Still open: …`, **listing only what is actionable in this session, never a future-dated item, one filed to run on its own, one blocked behind either, or anything the owner deferred away** (this rule was updated mid-session).
   - Link every issue, PR and source-controlled document named in conversation.
   - Open the pull request straight after committing, unasked.
   - `Comment class:` line opens the first substantive reply, class **alone on its line**.
   - Acting on an approval to merge applies only backward, never to anything requested or done after it.
   - Every GitHub comment/review/issue ends with the attribution footer (blank line, `---`, `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_`).
   - Commits end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` and `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CuwNWgfVqj6p3ehmvUXfTd`; PR bodies end with the 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code] lines plus the session URL.
   - **No model identifier in any repository artifact — chat replies only.** (Note: the owner's Model-field answer creates a deliberate, owner-authorised exception for the provenance `Model:` field specifically.)
   - The user's email `[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL]` is for identification/attribution only; never send it to an unrelated service.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**

   - **Claudinite** — pack-based instruction framework; unit of adoption is the *repository*, declaring packs in `.claudinite-settings.json`.
   - **Provenance convention** — one append-only file per carrier at `packs/<pack>/provenance/<element-id>.md`, holding *decisions*, never restating the rule. `_pack.md` for the manifest, `_declined.md` for turned-down candidates, `VERSIONS.md` under `provenance/`.

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs`** — the CLI. Read-only this segment. Key lines found:
     - Line 296: `const MODEL_TRAILER = /^co-authored-by:\s*(Claude\b[^<]*?)\s*</i;`

     ```js
     // Adds the `Model:` line to backfilled provenance entries, deriving it exactly as
     // provenance.mjs does (MODEL_TRAILER + the >1 generic-Claude drop) so these packs
     // spell it the same way as the rest of the shelf. An entry whose commit carries no
     // trailer gets no line: an unknown model is a state, never a guess.
     import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
     import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';

     const [root, dir] = process.argv.slice(2);
     const git = (...a) => execFileSync('git', ['-C', root, ...a], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 1 << 28 });
     const MODEL_TRAILER = /^co-authored-by:\s*(Claude\b[^<]*?)\s*</i;

     const byPr = new Map();
     for (const rec of git('log', 'main', '--format=%H%x00%s%x00%b%x01').split('\x01')) {
       const [sha, subject, body] = rec.replace(/^\n/, '').split('\x00');
       if (!sha) continue;
       // A squash names its pull request in the subject's tail; a merge commit names it up
       // front and carries no trailer of its own, so its models come off the branch side.
       const m = /\(#(\d+)\)\s*$/.exec(subject ?? '') ?? /^Merge pull request #(\d+)\b/.exec(subject ?? '');
       if (!m) continue;
       const models = new Set();
       for (const l of (body ?? '').split('\n')) {
         const t = MODEL_TRAILER.exec(l.trim());
         if (t) models.add(t[1].trim());
       }
       if (!models.size || (models.size === 1 && models.has('Claude'))) {
         const parents = git('rev-list', '--parents', '-n', '1', sha).trim().split(/\s+/).slice(1);
         if (parents.length > 1) {
           for (const l of git('log', '--format=%b', `${parents[0]}..${sha}`).split('\n')) {
             const t = MODEL_TRAILER.exec(l.trim());
             if (t) models.add(t[1].trim());
           }
         }
       }
       if (models.size > 1) models.delete('Claude');
       if (!byPr.has(m[1])) byPr.set(m[1], [...models]);
     }
     // ...per-file entry walk: buffers each `## `-headed entry, finds `**Landed:** #N`,
     // splices `- **Model:** <names>, per the commit trailer.` after the Actor field
     // (skipping the Actor's wrapped continuation lines), writes the file back.
     ```

Includes `notarized-build-should.md`, a file the subagent **invented** for an element no carrier names (retired into README prose at #1667, so the marking pass could never open it).    - **`packs/basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md`** — read and run three times (once per merge). Its test order: (1) can you watch it now? (2) did a test that ran prove it? (3) does it have an observable effect at all? (4) otherwise, where does its effect first become observable?

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/merge-to-main

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); when the change has an issue,
   the body carries `Closes #<issue>` on its own line.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
6. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read an issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

The merge leaves the local checkout on the branch it squashed, and no step here syncs `main`; the
merge is usually a session's last act. Only if you go on to start further work in this session,
sync first, before branching off anything:

```
git fetch origin main && git checkout main && git reset --hard origin/main && git remote prune origin
```
